tagline: Come for the food, stay for the vibe, return for the magic
geo_source: https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?q=480%20Hartz%20Ave%2C%20Danville%2C%20CA%2094526&format=json (returned OSM way 982722700, still labeled with the predecessor business "The Vine and Spirits", 480 Hartz Avenue, Danville 94526 — same building)
cuisine: Hawaiian / island-inspired comfort food with a classic tiki cocktail bar
description: Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar opened in April 2025 at 480 Hartz Ave in downtown Danville, in the space that was formerly The Vine and Spirits wine bar. Veteran Danville restaurateur Randy Negi (longtime owner of Bridges and a partner at Danville Brewing Company) built the concept around family trips to Hawaii and named it for his granddaughter Kaia, whose painted portrait greets guests near the entrance. The menu is food-first Hawaiian comfort fare — Spam musubi, poke crisps and bowls, loco moco, chicken katsu, kalbi beef, macadamia-crusted catch and a shareable Hula Pie — paired with a serious tiki program (a '44 Mai Tai, Ohanapod Mai Tai, Chi Chi, Zombie, Navy Grog, rum flights) assembled with help from Danville Brewing head brewer Matt Sager. The room mixes bamboo, thatch, carved tiki statues, blown-glass orbs, a sunset beach mural and colorful lighting, with an island garden patio (heaters and tiki torches), a reservable "Celi's Beach Hut," daily brunch and lunch, a keiki menu, and live Hawaiian music on Fridays.
owner_chef: Owner: Randy Negi (local restaurateur; former longtime owner of Bridges Restaurant, partner at Danville Brewing Company). Cocktail menu led by Matt Sager, head brewer at Danville Brewing Company. No named executive chef found.
opened: April 2025 (Diablo Magazine, 3/18/2025: planned launch "second week of April" 2025, dinner first then lunch and weekend brunch; mytiki.life and Yelp: reopened April 2025 after remodel of The Vine and Spirits; Town of Danville mayor welcome visit posted 6/27/2025)

yelp_rating: 3.9 (approx. 235-237 reviews; Yelp page title Sept 2026 says 235 reviews, Apple Maps' Yelp feed says 3.9/237)
brand_colors_or_style: Logo is a bold, all-caps, slightly distressed serif wordmark "KAIA'S" in dark olive (logo.png, ~#494714). The SpotHopper-built site uses a warm cream ground (#f3efe5) with dark-olive text (#494714 / #46430f) and bright tropical accents: palm green #66b95f (dominant), sunny yellow #ffde59, teal #52acaf, sunset orange #e58747, orchid purple #cb6ce6, with a rust-brown #a4664c nav hover. Type is Jost and Lexend Deca (clean geometric sans) with Agdasima/Poppins accents; all-caps headline copy ("SIP THE TROPICS, WALK THE DREAM", "MEET US UNDER THE PALMS"). Photography and decor: thatched-roof bar, a "fiery sunset" beach-and-palms wall mural, bamboo trim, carved tiki statues, blown-glass orbs, colorful lighting, tiki mugs, a fire-pit table, palm-lined garden patio with tiki torches. Mood: playful, saturated, family-friendly tropical escape rather than a dark dive-tiki look.
notes: Not found / could not verify: Google star rating (Google Maps place page returned only the generic shell; place_id ChIJfxrE3quMj4ARVZRm43itrZc comes from the site's own Get Directions link). Yelp's own page returned a bot-block, so the 3.9 rating comes from Yelp's page title in search results plus the Yelp-sourced Apple Maps listing. Tripadvisor page was blocked; a search snippet shows it "rated 5.0 of 5, #69 of 106 restaurants in Danville" but review count is unknown. Resy page is a JS shell (no hours/notes readable). DoorDash and Uber Eats store pages returned 403/Cloudflare; the links are from search results (titles confirm Kaia's, Danville). Instagram bio (from search snippet, ~2,572 followers): "an island-inspired escape with the spirit of Aloha... Restaurant and full bar. Family friendly. Open daily." Price range "$$$$" is what Yelp lists; actual menu runs $9-$19 starters, $16-$31 entrees, $16-$18 cocktails, which reads more like $$-$$$. The Toast gift card link still uses the old Vine slug: https://www.toasttab.com/the-vine-new-480-hartz-avenue/giftcards. Toast online-ordering closes at 8 PM (delivery/takeout 11:30 AM-8 PM on the day checked), earlier than dine-in hours. Diablo Magazine (3/18/2025) says the space is the former annex to Bridges; owner Negi is of Japanese descent and describes Kaia's as "a restaurant first." The Bay Area Telegraph reviewer noted only recorded ukulele music on their visit, but the official specials page lists live music every Friday 6-10 PM. Dog-friendly is based solely on Yelp's "Pets welcome" amenity. Catering is marked true but note the site says to-go catering trays are "coming soon." No TikTok found. No chef named anywhere; the cocktail list credit (Matt Sager) is from Diablo Magazine.
